package_info.package_versions: Unknown (latest version at time of campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: FlixOnline is a malicious Android application that impersonates a legitimate Netflix content enabler. It abuses Android permissions to intercept WhatsApp messages, automatically replies to contacts with malicious links to propagate itself, exfiltrates sensitive user data (contacts and SMS), and can download further payloads, exhibiting worm-like self-propagation and spyware behaviors.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, after installation and upon user granting requested permissions
execution_context.file_location: Main application code, likely within MainActivity.java or a persistent background service implementing NotificationListenerService

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The app requests permissions to overlay on top of other apps, read and send SMS, and access WhatsApp notifications. It registers a NotificationListenerService to monitor incoming WhatsApp messages. When a WhatsApp message is received, the app automatically replies to the sender with a message containing a malicious link to download the FlixOnline APK, enabling the malware to propagate to new victims.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the user grants permissions, the code registers a NotificationListenerService to monitor WhatsApp notifications, intercepts incoming messages, and automatically sends replies containing a malicious APK download link to the sender, resulting in self-propagation and further malware distribution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and replying to WhatsApp messages without user interaction, especially with links to malicious APKs, is a clear sign of automated malware propagation and abuse of messaging platforms.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Android apps do not monitor or auto-reply to WhatsApp messages, nor do they use messaging platforms to distribute malicious payloads or propagate themselves.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some accessibility or automation apps may interact with notifications for productivity or accessibility purposes, but they do not send unsolicited messages containing malware download links.
key_indicators: Abuse of NotificationListenerService to access WhatsApp message content
Automatic generation and sending of WhatsApp replies containing external APK download links
Requesting SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW (overlay) and notification access permissions without clear user benefit
Presence of code that programmatically interacts with WhatsApp notifications

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, after installation and upon user granting permissions
execution_context.file_location: Background service or broadcast receiver within the APK, likely a persistent service running in the background

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The app reads the user's contact list and SMS messages from the device using the appropriate Android APIs. It then establishes a network connection to a remote command and control (C2) server and uploads the exfiltrated contact and SMS data, enabling the attacker to harvest sensitive personal information.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the user grants permissions, the code accesses the device's contact list and SMS messages, then transmits this data via HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to a remote attacker-controlled server, resulting in unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive user information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating personal data such as contacts and SMS messages to an external server is a hallmark of spyware and data theft, especially when performed without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps do not send sensitive user data (contacts, SMS) to unknown remote servers without explicit user consent and a clear, user-facing purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or synchronization apps may upload contacts/SMS to reputable cloud services, but only with clear user consent and to well-known, trusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Network communication to unknown or suspicious C2 server endpoints
Access to and exfiltration of sensitive user data (contacts, SMS) without user awareness
Background service persisting after installation to harvest and transmit data
No legitimate user-facing reason for remote data transmission

attack_chain.action: User installs the FlixOnline app from the Google Play Store, believing it to be a legitimate Netflix content enabler.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is installed on the device and initiates permission requests.

attack_chain.action: App requests overlay, SMS, contacts, and notification access permissions from the user.
attack_chain.leads_to: App gains the ability to monitor WhatsApp notifications and access sensitive data on the device.

attack_chain.action: App registers a NotificationListenerService to monitor WhatsApp notifications and automatically replies to incoming messages with a malicious APK download link.
attack_chain.leads_to: Propagation to new victims via WhatsApp auto-replies containing malicious links.

attack_chain.action: App reads the user's contacts and SMS messages and exfiltrates this data to a remote command and control server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to sensitive user data.

attack_chain.action: App may receive instructions from the C2 server to download and execute additional malicious payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further compromise of the device or network, potentially enabling additional attacks or persistence.

behavioral_signatures: Android app requesting SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW (overlay), SMS, contacts, and notification access permissions without a clear, legitimate purpose
Registration and use of NotificationListenerService to monitor WhatsApp notifications
Automatic replies to WhatsApp messages containing external APK download links
Background exfiltration of contacts and SMS data to remote servers
file_indicators: APK package named 'FlixOnline' or similar variants
Presence of code referencing NotificationListenerService and WhatsApp package identifiers
Unusual background services with persistent network activity
Manifest entries requesting SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to unknown or suspicious C2 domains/IP addresses
Frequent POST requests containing contact or SMS data payloads
Connections initiated shortly after installation or permission grant
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications that request excessive permissions (overlay, SMS, contacts, notification access) without clear justification. Detect registration and use of NotificationListenerService targeting WhatsApp notifications. Analyze outgoing network traffic for exfiltration of contacts or SMS data to unknown servers, especially via POST requests. Flag apps that automatically generate WhatsApp replies containing APK download links. Use mobile security solutions to identify notification listener abuse, self-propagation behaviors, and unauthorized data exfiltration.
